title: The Relationship Between the Online Banking Usage and Financial Decision-Making Processes among Financial Management Students in Rural Areas
venue: International Journal of Sustainability and Advanced Integrated Research
tldr: Online banking trust and security show strong positive correlation with financial decision-making, while frequency of use shows moderate negative association among rural Filipino students.
problem_and_motivation: Online banking is increasingly embedded in daily life, but its relationship with financial decision-making among rural students with developing financial competencies is unclear.
approach: Descriptive-correlational quantitative design with 242 purposively selected Financial Management students in a rural area.
Guided by Technology Acceptance Model, Theory of Planned Behavior, and Financial Socialization Theory.
Measures online banking utilization: frequency, transaction type, and trust/security.
Assesses financial decision-making: budgeting, saving, and spending patterns.
findings: Low overall frequency of online banking use (overall mean=2.04, Rarely).
Transaction diversity (rs=.657 to .702, p=.000) showed strong positive association with financial decision-making.
Trust and security (rs=.753 to .823, p=.000) showed very strong positive associations.
Frequency of use showed significant moderate negative associations (rs=-.276 to -.282, p=.000).

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper demonstrates that trust and security are the strongest correlates of sound financial decision-making among rural students using online banking. It reveals a nuanced relationship where transaction diversity and trust matter more than mere usage frequency.
directly_justifies: Trust and security show very strong positive correlation with financial decision-making (rs=.753-.823).
Transaction diversity shows strong positive association (rs=.657-.702).
Frequency of online banking use shows moderate negative association with financial decision-making.
limits: Sample limited to Financial Management students in one rural area.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 1.A, 1.C, 2.A, 7.A, 13.A, 10.A (high). Rejected algorithmic topics (4.B-6.B, 8.A-9.C, 11.A-14.C) as this is a survey-based behavioral study.

limitations: Sample limited to Financial Management students in one rural area.
Self-reported data may introduce response bias.
remember_this: Trust and security strongly correlate with financial decision-making (rs up to .823).
Transaction diversity matters more than usage frequency.
Frequency of use shows negative association with decision-making.
